items.statement: With F, S, p, G as in the standard assumptions of §1 (F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, S ⊇ S_p all split in F), and each Θ_ṽ in (5) of order p: Let n ≥ 3 odd, p > 2n and π RACSDC on GL_n(𝔸_F) with (1) π ι-ordinary; (2) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1; (3) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n with χ_i^c = χ_i^∨ϵ^{1−n} and χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} of order > 2n; (4) r̄_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_ṽ}} trivial and [F_ṽ : ℚ_p] > n(n − 1)/2 + 1 at v ∈ S_p; (5) R = R_1 ⊔ R_2 ⊂ S − S_p non-empty of odd residue characteristic with π_ṽ|_{q_ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) (n_1 = 3, q_v a primitive 3rd root of unity mod p, on R_1; n_1 = n − 2, q_v a primitive (n − 2)th root, on R_2) and the splitting condition (d). For a place v_{St} above S − (S_p ∪ R) with q_{v_{St}} ≡ 1 mod p and r̄ trivial there, there is a RACSDC ι-ordinary π′ of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, HT_τ(r_{π′,ι}) = HT_τ(r_{π,ι}) for all τ, and π′_{v_{St}} an unramified twist of Steinberg.
items.note: Template: Clozel–Thorne 2017 Theorem 5.1. Proof: Lemma 6.7 gives a generic prime of the big ordinary Hecke algebra; Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 4.1 and Theorem 5.2 compare R_{D_{1,a}} and R_{D_{1,b}}; Geraghty Lemma 2.25 and Theorem 1.2 produce π″, and Lemma 6.2 with Proposition 5.8 descend. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): the standing assumptions and the order of Θ_ṽ were added; the 'Theorem 5.2' of the note is this paper's Theorem 5.2.

items.name: Lemma 6.2(1)–(2): Schur and primitive after Y_a-split extensions
items.statement: For a Y_a-split finite CM extension L/F (Y_a chosen so that such L are disjoint from the field cut out by r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}}): (1) r̄|_{G_{L⁺(ζ_p)}} is Schur; (2) r̄|_{G_L} is primitive.

items.name: Lemma 6.2(3)–(4): soluble base changes stay cuspidal
items.statement: (3) If L/F is soluble, the base change of π to L is cuspidal. (4) More generally if L/F_0/F with L/F_0 soluble and Π is RACSDC on GL_n(𝔸_{F_0}) with r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ r̄|_{G_{F_0}}, the base change of Π to L is cuspidal.
items.note: A non-cuspidal cyclic base change would make r_{Π_{F_1},ι} induced (Arthur–Clozel Theorems 4.2, 5.1, Proposition 4.4; Clozel's purity lemma), contradicting primitivity.

items.name: Lemma 6.3: auxiliary places with scalar residual Frobenius
items.statement: There are infinitely many prime-to-S places ṽ_a of F not split in F(ζ_p) with r̄(Frob_{ṽ_a}) scalar.
items.note: Chebotarev with τ = τ_0τ_0^c, ϵ(τ_0)² ≠ 1.

items.name: Deformation data D and Lemma 6.4
items.statement: A deformation datum D = (L, {R_v}_{v∈X}) is a Y_a ∪ S̃_a-split soluble CM L/F with X ⊂ S_L − S_{p,L} (with X̃ ⊂ S̃_L) and, for v ∈ X, R_v = R(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, r̄|_{G_{L_ṽ}}) (v ∈ R_L with ṽ split over F), the unipotent ring R^1_v or the Steinberg ring R^{St}_v (q_v ≡ 1 mod p, r̄ trivial); 𝒮_D = (L/L⁺, S_{p,L} ∪ X, …, Λ_L, r̄|_{G_{L⁺}}, ϵ^{1−n}δ^n, {R^Δ_v}_{S_{p,L}} ∪ {R_v}_X) with representing ring R_D. Lemma 6.4: every irreducible component of R_D has dimension ≥ 1 + n[L⁺ : ℚ].
items.note: Thorne 2015 Proposition 3.9 and Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 2.1.7. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): the paper prints X ⊂ S − S_p (sourceIssues E26); X is a set of places of L⁺.

items.name: Geraghty's big ordinary Hecke algebras and Proposition 6.5
items.statement: For a deformation datum D: U_D and the smooth 𝒪[U_D]-module M_D (lattices in ι^{−1}λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n)^∨ on q_ṽ at R-places, Iwahori level with trivial coefficients at R^1/R^{St} places), U(D, c) with Iw_ṽ(c, c) at p and K_ṽ(1) at ṽ_a, 𝕋^{ord}(D, c) ⊂ End S^{ord}(U(D, c), M_D) generated by the T^j_w and diamond operators, 𝕋^{ord}(D) = lim_c 𝕋^{ord}(D, c) and H^{ord}(D) = lim_c Hom(S^{ord}(U(D, c), M_D), 𝒪), with Geraghty's Λ_L-algebra structure. Proposition 6.5: H^{ord}(D) is a finite free Λ_L-module and 𝕋^{ord}(D), if non-zero, a finite faithful Λ_L-algebra.
items.locator: §6, pp. 89–90 (U_D and M_D p. 89; Proposition 6.5 p. 90)
items.note: As Geraghty Proposition 2.20 and Corollary 2.21 (U(D, 1) sufficiently small).

items.name: Lemma 6.6: the map from the deformation ring to the Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let 𝕋_D = 𝕋^{ord}(D)_{m_D} (m_D generated by m_{Λ_L} and T^j_w − q_w^{j(j−1)/2}tr ∧^j r̄(Frob_w)) and P_D ⊂ R_D the Λ_L-subalgebra generated by characteristic-polynomial coefficients (R_D finite over P_D, Thorne 2015 Propositions 3.26, 3.29). If R_v ≠ R^{St}_v for all v ∈ X, there is a natural surjection P_D → 𝕋_D of Λ_L-algebras; J_D denotes its kernel.
items.note: As Thorne 2015 Proposition 4.12, via Galois representations r_σ over rings A_c (Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemmas 2.1.5, 2.1.7).

items.name: Lemma 6.7: a generic prime unramified outside p
items.statement: There is a deformation datum D_1 = (L_1, ∅) with 𝕋_{D_1} ≠ 0 and a generic prime p_1 ⊂ R_{D_1} of dimension 1 and characteristic p with J_{D_1} ⊂ p_1 and r_{p_1}|_{G_{L_1,v_{St}}} trivial.
items.note: Proof: an R̃ ∪ Y_a ∪ {ṽ_a}-split soluble L_0 with d_{R_i,L_0} > n + n² (cyclic M_d as in Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 7.1; Maire Proposition 19), Theorem 1.4 and Theorem 5.7 at L_0, then L_1 where the types become unramified (Proposition 1.22(4)) and Thorne 2015 Proposition 4.18.

items.name: The CM newform σ_0 of weight 5 and level Γ_1(4)
items.statement: σ_0 is the cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of the normalised newform f_0 = q − 4q² + 16q⁴ − 14q⁵ − 64q⁸ + ⋯ of level Γ_1(4) and weight 5, the automorphic induction from K = ℚ(i) of the unramified Hecke character of ∞-type (4, 0). For p ≡ 1 mod 4, σ_0 is ι-ordinary, r_{σ_0,ι} ≅ Ind^{G_ℚ}_{G_K}ψ and det r_{σ_0,ι} = δ_{K/ℚ}ϵ^{−4}.

items.name: Theorem 7.1: residually CM symmetric powers with a Steinberg place
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3, p ≡ 1 mod 48n!, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, q ≠ p a prime, X_0 a finite set of places of K prime to 2pq and ω : G_K → Q̄_p^× de Rham with ωω^c = ϵ³ and ω unramified on X_0. Then there are an X_0-split soluble CM extension F/K and a RACSDC ι-ordinary Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) with (a) r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ ω̄^{n−1}|_{G_F} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_F}, (b) HT_τ(r_{Π,ι}) = HT_τ(ω^{n−1}|_{G_F} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_F}) for all τ, and (c) Π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg at some v | q.
items.note: Odd n is Proposition 7.4; n = 2^r m follows by induction on r from Anastassiades–Thorne Theorem 5.1 applied to π_0 = π_1 ⊞ π_2 with r_{π_0} ≅ ω^{2n−1} ⊗ Sym^{2n−1}r_{σ_0}. Remark 7.5: for n a power of 2, Anastassiades–Thorne alone suffices. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): the printed proof of the odd case (Proposition 7.4, item 120) applies Theorem 4.1 to a π_2 that is not conjugate self-dual (sourceIssues E21), so the printed proof covers Theorem 7.1 only for n a power of 2 (Remark 7.5, via Anastassiades–Thorne alone). No counterexample to the theorem is known.

items.name: Lemma 7.2: properties of the residual symmetric powers
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3, p ≡ 1 mod 48n!, ω de Rham with ωω^c = ϵ³, F/K finite CM linearly disjoint from the extension of K(ζ_p) cut out by r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_{K(ζ_p)}}, and χ_i = ω̄^{n−1} ⊗ ψ̄^{n−i}(ψ̄^c)^{i−1}, ρ̄ = ⊕χ_i ≅ ω̄^{n−1} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_K}. Then (1) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1; (2) ψ̄/ψ̄^c|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has order > 2n(n − 1) and χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} order > 2n; (3) χ_iχ_i^c = ϵ^{1−n}; (4) ζ_p ∉ F^{ker ad ρ̄} and F ⊄ F⁺(ζ_p); (5) ρ̄|_{G_F} is primitive.

items.name: Corollary 7.3: a weight-5 form with automorphic symmetric power
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 there is a cuspidal σ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 5, unramified away from 2 and a prime q ≡ 3 mod 4, with σ_2 ≅ i^{GL_2}_{B_2}χ_1 ⊗ χ_2 (χ_1 unramified, χ_2 of conductor 4), σ_q an unramified twist of Steinberg, and Sym^{n−1}r_{σ,ι} automorphic for every p and ι.
items.note: Proof: q ≡ 3 mod 4, q ≡ −1 mod p; level raising for GL_2 (Diamond 1989 Corollary 6.9); Theorem 7.1; Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 6.1 (hypotheses from Lemma 7.2) and soluble descent.

items.name: Level raising for GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) (Diamond 1989; Diamond–Taylor 1994) and Edixhoven's ordinarity criterion
items.statement: Diamond 1989 Corollary 6.9 raises the level of a form at a prime q satisfying the level-raising congruence to an unramified Steinberg twist at q; Diamond–Taylor 1994 Theorem A produces forms with prescribed supercuspidal or Steinberg components at non-optimal levels with the same residual representation; a form unramified at p with reducible residual representation at p, Hodge–Tate weights (0, 8k) and p > 8k is ι-ordinary (Edixhoven 1992 Theorem 2.6).
items.locator: §7, proofs of Corollary 7.3 and Proposition 7.4, pp. 96, 98–99
items.note: Imported GL_2 inputs. The atlas has the Ihara lemma (ModularCurvesPartII R14.4) and level lowering (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2) but no level-raising theorem; CT17's Part II records the same gap. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): Edixhoven's criterion needs level prime to p (a form Steinberg at p has slope (k − 2)/2); here τ is unramified outside 2, q_1, q_2 (p. 98).

items.name: Proposition 7.4: Theorem 7.1 for odd n
items.statement: Theorem 7.1 holds when n = 2k + 1 is odd.
items.note: Proof by induction on odd n: Chebotarev primes q_1 (split in K, > n, q_1 a primitive 6th root of unity mod p, Frobenius ratios q_1^{±1} on Ind ψ̄^{2k} and a primitive 12k-th root on Ind ψ̄), q_2 ≡ −1 and q_3 (primitive (n − 2)th root); real quadratic M_1, M_2, M_3; a GL_2 form τ (Diamond–Taylor) Steinberg at q_1 and supercuspidal at q_2; the inductive π on GL_{n−2}; Proposition 5.8 (fixed-type rings, Shotton Definition 3.5), Theorem 4.1, the stronger property at q_1, L_1 = L_0K (Arthur–Clozel Theorem 4.2) and Theorem 6.1. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): sourceIssues E21: π_2 = τ_0 ⊗ |·|^{(n−2)/2}ιω_1ω_0^{n−1} is not conjugate self-dual; it fails by δ_{K/ℚ}|_{G_{F_0}}. The hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 are therefore not met as claimed on p. 100. See also E22 (Lemma 6.7), E19 (the base case n = 3) and E23 (Hodge–Tate weights).

items.name: Level raising for GL_{2n} of unitary type (Anastassiades–Thorne, Theorem 5.1)
items.statement: Given cuspidal conjugate self-dual π_1, π_2 on GL_n(𝔸_F) whose isobaric sum π_0 = π_1 ⊞ π_2 is regular algebraic and ι-ordinary, with r_{π_0,ι} := r_{π_1|·|^{−n/2},ι} ⊕ r_{π_2|·|^{−n/2},ι} satisfying local–global compatibility at every finite place, and with the p-adic places and the ramified places of π split over F⁺, with π_i ≅ St_n(ξ_i) at a place v, ι^{−1}ξ_1/ξ_2(ϖ_v) ≡ q_v^n mod m, and r̄ not a twist of 1 ⊕ ϵ^{−1} ⊕ ⋯, there are a soluble X_0-split quadratic CM F′/F and a RACSDC ι-ordinary π′ of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{F′}) with r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π_0,ι}|_{G_{F′}}, the same weight, and an unramified twist of Steinberg at a place above v.
items.note: Imported from Anastassiades–Thorne, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu (2021); it passes from Sym^{n−1} to Sym^{2n−1}. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): statement corrected against p. 102: π_0 is an isobaric sum, not cuspidal, and the hypotheses the paper checks were stated.

items.name: Proposition 8.2: symmetric powers with n-regular refinements at ramified primes
items.statement: Let π be cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2, not CM, with an n-regular accessible refinement at every prime where it is ramified. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every ι.
items.note: Proof by induction on the number of primes dividing the conductor: at a ramified p, move along the tame level M, p-adic eigencurve (avoiding the closed set of Lemma 2.35) to a classical π′ of level prime to p, then Theorem 2.33 (ordinary or non-ordinary case).

items.name: Proposition 8.3: a congruence to a form with n-regular refinements
items.statement: Let π be cuspidal of weight k ≥ 2 without CM, with non-trivial Jacquet module at every l. There are p, ι and π′ cuspidal of weight k with (1) p > max(2(n + 1), (n − 1)k); (2) r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) ⊇ a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_p); (3) π_p, π′_p unramified; (4) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}; (5) every π′_l has non-trivial Jacquet module, and every accessible refinement of π′_l is n-regular where π′_l is ramified.
items.note: Proof by Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching (Kisin Proposition 3.2.5; Thorne 2016 Definition 5.6, Theorem 5.9, Propositions 5.10, 6.5, Lemma 6.8; Khare–Thorne Corollary 2.7, Lemma 2.8; Thorne 2012 Lemma 6.10): if every congruent form failed n-regularity the patched module would live on the codimension-one quotient by I = ∏I_l, contradicting dim H_∞ = 4|T| + q_0. Weston's unobstructedness and Diamond–Taylor Lemma 11 choose p and q_a.

items.name: Lemma 8.4: the non-regular locus of a local lifting ring is a principal divisor
items.statement: For l ∈ S − {p} and a Frobenius lift φ_l there is a principal ideal I_l ⊂ R_l (the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of Sym^{n−1}r_l^{univ}(φ_l)) such that a Q̄_p-point f has eigenvalues α_l, β_l of ρ_f(φ_l) with (α_l/β_l)^i = 1 for some 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1 iff f(I_l) = 0, and dim R_l/I_l < dim R_l.
items.note: Uses that π_l has non-trivial Jacquet module, R_l formally smooth of relative dimension 3, and Gee 2011 Proposition 2.1.5.

items.name: Patching data for modular curves with Fontaine–Laffaille condition at p
items.statement: The deformation problem 𝒮 = (ρ̄, χ, S, {𝒪}, {D_v}) (Fontaine–Laffaille lifts of determinant χ with the same Hodge–Tate weights as r_{π,ι} at p, all lifts elsewhere), H = H¹(Y_{U_1(Mq_a)}, Sym^{k−2}𝒪²) with Hecke algebra 𝕋^S and R_𝒮 → 𝕋^S_m surjective, Taylor–Wiles sets Q_N (q ≡ 1 mod p^N, distinct Frobenius eigenvalues, |Q_N| = q_0), Δ_Q, augmented problems 𝒮_Q, H_{Q,m_{Q,1}} free over 𝒪[Δ_Q] with H_{Q,m_{Q,1}} ⊗_{𝒪[Δ_Q]} 𝒪 ≅ H_m, framed rings R^T and presentations A^T_𝒮[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R_{𝒮^T_{Q_N}} with g = q_0 + |T| − 1. Patching gives S_∞ = 𝒯⟦S_1, …, S_{q_0}⟧ → R_∞ = (A^T/I)⟦X_1, …, X_g⟧ and a finite R_∞-module H_∞ free over S_∞ (Thorne 2012 Lemma 6.10), of the same dimension over R_∞ and S_∞ (Khare–Thorne 2017 Lemma 2.8).
items.note: Auxiliary levels and freeness are GL2ModularityLifting R22.2, arithmetic patching R22.3. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): the localisation, the Hodge–Tate condition and the patching conclusion were added (pp. 107–110); the abstract patching and the dimension comparison are R03.5 and R03.3.

items.name: Soluble base change and descent for GL_n (Arthur–Clozel)
items.statement: Cyclic base change and automorphic induction for GL_n and the resulting soluble descent: if F/ℚ is a soluble Galois extension, ρ|_{G_F} is irreducible and automorphic, then ρ is automorphic.
items.locator: §2, proof of Theorem 2.33, p. 59; §6, Lemma 6.2; §7, pp. 97, 101
items.note: ML.5 registers cyclic base change and automorphic induction. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21): the cyclic base change dichotomy the paper also uses in §6 and on p. 101 (Arthur–Clozel Theorem 4.2) is now item 163.

items.name: Regular algebraic, weight λ, conjugate self-dual, polarizable and RACSDC representations
items.statement: An automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) (F CM or totally real) is regular algebraic if π_∞ has the infinitesimal character of an irreducible algebraic representation W of (Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n)_ℂ, of weight λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,ℂ)} if W^∨ has highest weight λ; it is conjugate self-dual if π^c ≅ π^∨, and then (π, δ^n_{F/F⁺}) is polarized; polarizable is as in BLGGT14 §2.1; RACSDC means regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual and cuspidal.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. AG2.0: 'Define regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual, essentially conjugate self-dual and polarized cases separately, retaining the multiplier character'.

items.name: Galois characters of algebraic Hecke characters
items.statement: For a Hecke character χ : F^×\𝔸_F^× → ℂ^× of type A_0 and ι : Q̄_p → ℂ there is a continuous character r_{χ,ι} : G_F → Q̄_p^×, de Rham at v | p, with WD(r_{χ,ι}) ∘ Art_{F_v} = ι^{−1}χ|_{F_v^×} at every finite v; conversely every de Rham character unramified almost everywhere arises in this way (written χ = ιχ′).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. AG2.0 takes n = 1 algebraic Hecke characters as its acceptance example; AF.5 proves the GL_1 dictionary with Hecke characters including infinity type.

items.name: Weil–Deligne representations and the normalisation of Art_K
items.statement: For K/ℚ_l finite and ρ : G_K → GL_n(Q̄_p) continuous (de Rham if l = p), WD(ρ) = (r, N) is the associated Weil–Deligne representation and WD(ρ)^{F-ss} its Frobenius semisimplification; Art_K : K^× → W_K^{ab} sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenius elements.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. R01.2 constructs the Weil–Deligne representation and 'Distinguish[es] the full object, its semisimplification, and its Frobenius semisimplification'.

items.name: Normalised parabolic induction, products and isobaric sums for GL_n
items.statement: For a parabolic P = MN of GL_n(K), i^G_P(σ) = Ind(σ ⊗ δ_P^{1/2}) with δ_P(x) = |det(Ad(x)|_{Lie N_P})|; for the standard Levi L_{(n_i)} ⊂ P_{(n_i)}, π_1 × ⋯ × π_k = i^{GL_n}_{P_{(n_i)}}(π_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ π_k); the isobaric sum ⊞π_i is an irreducible subquotient of ×π_i.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. SR.2 defines 'normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character'; ET.6 the segment and Langlands-quotient theory. Used in items 16 and 55 and in Proposition 1.20.

items.name: The discrete spectrum of GL_m (Mœglin–Waldspurger)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [MW89].) Every discrete automorphic representation of GL_m(𝔸_F) is a Speh representation built from a cuspidal π_0 of GL_a(𝔸_F), m = ab; a non-cuspidal π_i (b ≥ 2) contributes to r_{σ,ι} a direct sum of b twists of one Galois representation by powers of the cyclotomic character.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. ET.7a: 'Develop the required GL_m residual-spectrum/Speh classification'.

items.name: Temperedness of cuspidal RACSDC representations
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [Shi11, Clo13, Car12].) A cuspidal RACSDC automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) is tempered at every finite place.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Follows from local–global compatibility with purity (AG2.5: 'monodromy-purity comparison … the Caraiani/Taylor–Yoshida upgrades'). The L-packets of §1.8 are defined only for tempered representations.

items.name: Endoscopic transfer of Deligne–Lusztig functions (Kazhdan–Varshavsky)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [KV12, Theorem 2.2.6].) If char k(v) > n, the transfer φ(v, θ, n)^H of the Deligne–Lusztig test function can be taken to be a weighted sum of inflations to H(𝒪) of the characters R^{H_{k(v)}}_{C_i}(θ^{−1} ⊗ ω(ṽ)^{⊗(k−1)}), one for each conjugacy class of embeddings C_i : C × Res_{k(ṽ)/k(v)}𝔾_m^{k−1} → H_{k(v)}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Named only in the note of item 30. ET.3 plans transfer and the fundamental lemma, not the explicit transfer of Deligne–Lusztig functions. Routed with the level-raising material (route 3).

items.name: The symmetric power lift Sym^{n−1}π
items.statement: For a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_2(𝔸_F), Sym^{n−1}π exists if there is an automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) whose Langlands parameter at every place v is the image of that of π_v under Sym^{n−1} : GL_2 → GL_n.
items.locator: Introduction, p. 1 (the functorial lift along R : GL_n → GL_N)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. For regular algebraic π over ℚ the paper passes between 'Sym^{n−1}π exists' (Theorems A, B) and 'Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic' (Theorems 7.7, 8.1). That passage uses local–global compatibility (item 7), strong multiplicity one and matching at infinity; it is not written out. Planned where PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B plans the same definition.

items.name: Modularity of semistable elliptic curves over ℚ
items.statement: Every semistable elliptic curve E over ℚ is modular (Wiles, Taylor–Wiles; every E/ℚ by Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor): there is a weight-2 cuspidal π_E of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of squarefree conductor N_E with r_{π_E,ι} ≅ H¹_ét(E_ℚ̄, ℚ_p) ⊗ Q̄_p; π_{E,l} is a twist of Steinberg for l | N_E, so Theorem B applies.
items.locator: Introduction, before Corollary C, p. 2 (used without citation)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. R29.6 states the unconditional modularity theorem with a weight-two newform of exact conductor.

items.name: Standard L-functions of cuspidal representations of GL_m are entire (Godement–Jacquet)
items.statement: For m ≥ 2 and a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_m(𝔸_F), the completed standard L-function Λ(s, Π) extends to an entire function with Λ(s, Π) = ε(s, Π)Λ(1 − s, Π^∨).
items.locator: Introduction, Corollary C, p. 2 (used without statement)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Corollary C applies it to Π = Sym^n π_E (item 135), whose Euler factors agree with those of Λ(Sym^n E, s) (item 137) at every prime by item 134 and local–global compatibility.

items.name: The completed symmetric power L-function Λ(Sym^n E, s)
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over ℚ and n ≥ 1, Λ(Sym^n E, s) is the product of the archimedean Γ-factor of Sym^n H¹(E(ℂ), ℚ) and the Euler factors det(1 − Frob_p p^{−s} | (Sym^n H¹_ét(E_ℚ̄, ℚ_l))^{I_p})^{−1} (l ≠ p), as defined e.g. in Dummigan–Martin–Watkins 2009.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. The paper refers to DMW09, and the review stated the standard definition. Planned as in PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B.

items.name: H⁰ of rank-one (φ, Γ)-modules over the Robba ring (KPX Proposition 6.2.8)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it.) For a continuous character δ : F_ṽ^× → E^×, H⁰_{φ,γ}(ℛ_{E,F_ṽ}(δ)) = 0 unless δ = x^{−a} = ∏_τ τ^{−a_τ} with a ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^{Hom(F_ṽ,E)}, and it is one-dimensional when δ is trivial.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. A local input of the trianguline theory of route 5.

items.name: Triangulations from Weil–Deligne filtrations of de Rham representations
items.statement: (As the paper uses it: Breuil–Schneider Proposition 4.1, Berger 2008, KPX Example 6.2.6(3).) For de Rham ρ_v, sub-WD representations of WD(ρ_v) correspond to sub-(φ, N, G)-modules of D_pst(ρ_v); Berger's tensor equivalence between filtered (φ, N, G)-modules and (φ, Γ)-modules restricts to D_pst ↔ D†_rig on de Rham representations, and a rank-one object with WD character χ and Hodge jumps a_τ corresponds to ℛ(x^{−a}(χ ∘ Art)). Hence a filtration of WD(ρ_v) with graded characters χ_{v,i} induces a triangulation of D†_rig(ρ_v).
items.locator: §2.3.1, proof of Lemma 2.8, p. 31; Example 2.10, pp. 32–33; proof of Lemma 2.29, pp. 51–52
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Local p-adic Hodge theory for route 5 (the trianguline variety's local foundations).

items.name: Bloch–Kato Selmer groups H¹_f and H¹_g
items.statement: For a de Rham representation V of G_{F_v}: H¹_f(F_v, V) = ker(H¹(F_v, V) → H¹(F_v, V ⊗ B_cris)) and H¹_g with B_dR for v | p, and H¹_f = H¹_ur for v ∤ p; globally H¹_f(F⁺, ad ρ) is the subgroup of classes that lie in H¹_f at every place.
items.locator: §2.3.1, Proposition 2.11(4), p. 34; proof of Theorem 2.24, p. 47
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Used in Proposition 2.11 and in item 73 but never defined in the paper. SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4 defines 'finite Bloch–Kato … local conditions' and PadicHodgeRegulators L1 constructs 'the finite local condition'.

items.name: Generic Weil–Deligne representations (Allen)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [All16, Definition 1.1.2].) A Frobenius-semisimple WD representation (r, N) is generic if Hom_{WD}((r, N), (r, N)(1)) = 0; this holds in particular when (r, N) is pure.
items.locator: §2.3.1, Proposition 2.11(2), p. 34; proof of Theorem 2.24, p. 47
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Stated as used (the paper checks it through purity). Belongs with the adjoint Selmer theory of route 7.

items.name: Local Bloch–Kato conditions at generic places (Allen, Remark 1.2.9)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it.) If WD(ρ_v) is generic, then H¹_f(F_v, ad ρ_v) = H¹_g(F_v, ad ρ_v) for v ∈ S_p with ρ_v de Rham, and H¹_f(F_v, ad ρ_v) = H¹(F_v, ad ρ_v) for v ∈ S − S_p.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 7, with item 141.

items.name: Accumulating non-critical points give trianguline points (BHS17 Lemme 2.11)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, in the published version of Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen 2017; footnote 5: the arXiv version is restricted to crystalline representations.) Let U be a connected affinoid with a family ρ^u_v and a parameter δ, trianguline of parameter δ on a Zariski open dense V ⊂ U, with numerically non-critical classical points accumulating at z. If δ_z = δ_alg·δ_sm is locally algebraic and every triangulation of ρ_z|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is non-critical, then δ_alg is strictly dominant and ρ_z is trianguline of parameter δ_z.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. An input of Lemma 2.30 (item 65); routed with it to the companion-points candidate (route 4).

items.name: Ordinary tangent vectors lie in H¹_g (Geraghty Lemma 3.9)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it.) Ordinary E[ε]-deformations whose parameter maps to 0 in the tangent space of weight space lie in H¹_g; with the vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups (item 73) this makes T_{z_n}Z^{ord} → T𝒲_n injective.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Geraghty's ordinary theory is in route 7.

items.name: Irreducible components of rigid spaces under base change (Conrad)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [Con99, Theorem 3.4.2].) Each irreducible component of X_{ℂ_p} lies in the base change of an irreducible component of X, and for some finite E′/E the irreducible components of X_{E′} are geometrically irreducible.
items.locator: §2.18.1, proof of Theorem 2.24, pp. 46–47; Corollary 2.28, footnote 4, p. 50; proof of Theorem 2.33, pp. 57–58
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. No layer plans it; routed with Lemma 2.2 (item 39) to route 2.

items.name: Jacquet modules of induced Steinberg representations (Zelevinsky)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [Zel80, Theorem 1.2].) The subquotients of the normalised Jacquet module of i_P(St_{n_1}(ψ_1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ St_{n_k}(ψ_k)) are exactly β_{w^{−1}(1)} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ β_{w^{−1}(n)} for the permutations w increasing on each block.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. SR.2 plans Jacquet functors and the geometric lemma; ET.6 the segment theory.

items.name: Irreducibility of principal series (Zelevinsky, Rodier)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [Zel80, Theorem 9.7] with [Rod82, §4.4].) If π_{n,v} is generic and rec^T(π_{n,v}) is a sum of characters no ratio of two of which is the norm character, then i_B(ιχ_{n,v}) is irreducible and isomorphic to π_{n,v}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. ET.6 develops the segment/Langlands-quotient classification.

items.name: Large image for non-CM modular forms (Ribet, Momose)
items.statement: Let π be a non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ). The Zariski closure of r_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) contains SL_2; and for all but finitely many primes p that split completely in the coefficient field of π, the image of r̄_{π,ι} contains a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_p).
items.locator: §2.31, Theorem 2.33 (2ord), p. 57; §8, proof of Proposition 8.3, p. 106 (used without citation)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Sources: K. Ribet, Glasgow Math. J. 27 (1985); F. Momose, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 28 (1981). Item 84 is only the local version. Routed as in PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B, as a source of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.3 (route 8).

items.name: The base-change morphism of the proof of Theorem 2.33
items.statement: With T̃ = 𝒯_0 ×_{𝒲_0} 𝒲̃ and b_p : T̃ → 𝒯_2 twisting by ψ^{−1}, the morphism b : 𝒳_{0,ps} × T̃ → 𝒳_{2,ps} × 𝒯_2, (τ, μ) ↦ (τ|_{G_F} ⊗ ψ^{−1}, b_p(μ)), satisfies: b ∘ ĩ sends classical points into i_2(ℰ_2), by Labesse's descent (Labesse Théorème 5.4).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 2, with Theorem 2.33 (item 76).

items.name: Congruence subgroups of the unit group (Chevalley)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [Che51, Théorème 1].) Every subgroup of finite index of the unit group 𝒪_F^× of a number field F contains the units congruent to 1 modulo some non-zero ideal.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 2, with Lemma 2.34 (item 77).

items.name: Primitive representations
items.statement: For a profinite group Γ, a field k and a continuous ρ̄ : Γ → GL_n(k), ρ̄ is primitive if it is not isomorphic to Ind_{Γ′}^{Γ} σ̄ for any proper closed subgroup Γ′ of finite index and any σ̄ : Γ′ → GL_{n/[Γ:Γ′]}(k).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. A hypothesis of the Allen–Newton–Thorne lifting theorems (Lemma 5.1, Theorem 5.2, Proposition 5.8(2), Lemmas 6.2, 7.2). Route 7.

items.name: Generic primes of an ordinary deformation ring (Allen–Newton–Thorne Definition 3.7)
items.statement: A prime 𝔭 ⊂ R_𝒮 of dimension 1 and characteristic p, with A = R_𝒮/𝔭 and r_𝔭 the pushforward of the universal deformation, is generic at p if for each v ∈ S_p the characters ψ^v_1, …, ψ^v_n : I^{ab}_{F_ṽ}(p) → A^× are distinct and for some v ∈ S_p and σ ∈ I^{ab}_{F_ṽ}(p) the values ψ^v_1(σ), …, ψ^v_n(σ) satisfy no non-trivial ℤ-linear relation; 𝔭 is generic if moreover r_𝔭|_{G_{F,S}} ⊗_A Frac A is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Used in Theorem 5.7 and in §6 (items 113–114). Route 7.

items.name: The level U and the types τ_g, λ_g of §4
items.statement: U = ∏U_v with: U_v arbitrary with π_ṽ^{ι_ṽ(U_v)} ≠ 0 at v ∈ S; G(𝒪_{F⁺_v}) at v ∉ S ∪ T; ι_ṽ^{−1}Iw_ṽ(c, c) at v ∈ S_p, with π_ṽ^{Iw_ṽ(c,c),ord} ≠ 0 and U_v torsion-free; ι_v^{−1}𝔭_v at v ∈ T_1; ι_ṽ^{−1}𝔮_ṽ at v ∈ T_2 ∪ T_3 (n_1 = 2 on T_2, n_1 = n − 2 on T_3). τ_g = ⊗_{T_1}τ(v, n) ⊗ ⊗_{T_2∪T_3}λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) and λ_g = ⊗_{T_1}λ(v, θ_v, n) ⊗ ⊗_{T_2∪T_3}λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) as ℂ[U]-modules, with 𝒪-lattices τ̊_g, λ̊_g; U_L, τ_{g,L}, λ_{g,L} likewise over L.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Used by Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.6 (items 89, 93). Route 3.

items.name: The BLGGT14 §1.1 operations on 𝒢_n-valued representations
items.statement: For ψ̄ : G_F → k^× with ψ̄ψ̄^c = ϵ^{1−2n}μ̄^{−1}|_{G_F}: (ψ̄, ϵ^{1−2n}μ̄^{−1}δ_{F/F⁺}) : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_1(k); r̄ ⊗ (ψ̄, …) : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(k) with multiplier ϵ^{1−2n}; r̄_1 = I(r̄ ⊗ (ψ̄, …)) : G_{F⁺} → GSp_{2n}(k); r̄_2 = (r̄_1)^∧_{G_F} : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_{2n}(k) with ν ∘ r̄_2 = ϵ^{1−2n}; r̄_1|_{G_F} and r̄_2|_{G_F} are conjugate to ρ̄ ⊗ ψ̄ ⊕ ρ̄^c ⊗ ψ̄^c; and the same operations on deformations give r′ with r′|_{G_L} = (r ⊗ ψ̄ ⊕ r^c ⊗ ψ̄^c)|_{G_L}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 7, with Theorem 5.2 (item 96).

items.name: The sign of the polarization (Bellaïche–Chenevier)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [BC11].) For π = π_2 ⊞ π_{n−2} as in §4, r_{π,ι} extends to r : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(Q̄_p) with ν ∘ r = ϵ^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. AG2.2 'recover[s] the specified polarization', and G7 proves the symmetry sign of a polarization.

items.name: Global lifts with prescribed local components (Bellovin–Gee Corollary 5.1.1)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, with the irreducibility hypothesis weakened to r̄|_{G_{F_0⁺(ζ_p)}} Schur, which is all the proof uses for the vanishing of H⁰(ad r̄) and H⁰(ad r̄(1)).) For r̄ : G_{F_0⁺,S_0} → 𝒢_n(k) with ν ∘ r̄ = ϵ^{1−n}δ^n_{F_0/F_0⁺}, and local rings R_v at the places above p (of dimension 1 + n² + n(n − 1)[F_{0,ṽ} : ℚ_p]/2), R̄_v at T_0, R^{St}_v at Σ_0 and the inertia-isomorphism components at inert places, the universal ring exists and has Krull dimension ≥ 1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 7, with Proposition 5.8 (item 102).

items.name: Lie algebras of Hodge–Tate representations (Sen)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [Sen73, Theorem 1].) If ρ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL_2(Q̄_p) is Hodge–Tate with distinct weights, a maximal torus of the Zariski closure of its image is regular in GL_2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. No layer plans Sen's theorem. Route 2, with item 84.

items.name: Mod 5 and mod 7 level-one eigenforms (as used in Lemma 3.4)
items.statement: For l ∈ {5, 7}, r̄^{ss}_{f,ι_l} of a level-one eigenform is a twist of the representation of a level-one eigenform of weight ≤ l + 1: E_4 or E_6 for l = 5, and E_4, E_6 or E_8 for l = 7. Hence ι_5^{−1}(α/β) ≡ 2³ or 2⁵ and ι_7^{−1}(α/β) ≡ 2³, 2⁵ or 2⁷ modulo 𝔪.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 2, with Lemma 3.4 (item 82).

items.name: Classical weights in the 2-adic boundary annulus
items.statement: For a classical point z of weight k with κ(z)(5) = 5^{k−2}ζ_{2^m}: κ(z) ∈ 𝒲_0(b) iff k is odd or m ≥ 1; v_2(w(z)) = 2^{1−m} for m ≥ 1 and v_2(w(z)) = 2 for m = 0 with k odd; and (k − 1)/v_2(w(z)) is an integer.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. The review checked it from v_2(5^j − 1) = 2 + v_2(j) and v_2(ζ_{2^m} − 1) = 2^{1−m}. Needed in Lemma 3.7 to get s(z′) = 2i and i′ = 2^m − 1. Route 2.

items.name: Unobstructedness for almost all p and the auxiliary prime q_a
items.statement: (As the paper uses it.) For non-CM π of conductor M and all but finitely many p: H⁰(ℚ_l, ad⁰r̄(1)) = 0 at every ramified l, so the fixed-determinant lifting rings there are formally smooth (Weston 2004, Propositions 3.2, 5.3); and there is a prime q_a > p with π_{q_a} unramified and a formally smooth lifting ring at q_a (Diamond–Taylor 1994, Lemma 11).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 2, with Proposition 8.3 (item 123).

items.name: Completed local rings at characteristic-zero points of lifting rings
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [Gee11, Proposition 2.1.5].) For a closed point x of R_l[1/p], the completed local ring pro-represents the lifts of the characteristic-zero representation ρ_x to Artinian E_x-algebras.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. R08.3 proves 'the characterisation of characteristic-zero points', and R03.4 the extraction of characteristic-zero points.

items.name: The auxiliary field L_0 of Lemma 6.7
items.statement: L_0 = M_d · F, where M_d/F⁺ is cyclic, totally real, of odd degree d > n + n², split at R, Y^a and S_a and totally inert at S_p; then d_{R_i,L_0} > n + n², [L_{0,ṽ} : ℚ_p] > n², and r̄ is trivial with q_v ≡ 1 mod p at the other places required (class field theory, Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 7.1, Maire Proposition 19).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Route 3. The multiplicity claim in its proof is recorded as sourceIssues E22.

items.name: Cyclic base change for GL_n (Arthur–Clozel)
items.statement: (As the paper uses it, [AC89, Theorem 4.2, Theorem 5.1, Proposition 4.4] with [Clo90b, Lemma 4.9].) For a cyclic extension F_1/F of prime degree l and cuspidal Π of GL_n(𝔸_F), the base change Π_{F_1} exists and is either cuspidal or of the form Ξ ⊞ Ξ^σ ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Ξ^{σ^{l−1}} with Ξ cuspidal on GL_{n/l}(𝔸_{F_1}); in particular it is cuspidal when l = 2 and n is odd.
items.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.2, p. 88; §7, proof of Proposition 7.4, p. 101
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Split from item 126. ET.7a develops 'cyclic automorphic-induction/base-change steps from the Arthur–Clozel … proofs, with central characters and cuspidality hypotheses'; ML.5 registers cyclic base change.

items.name: The Chebotarev density theorem
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields and a conjugacy class C of Gal(L/K), the set of primes of K unramified in L whose Frobenius class is C has Dirichlet density #C/#Gal(L/K); in particular it is infinite.
items.locator: §7, proof of Proposition 7.4, p. 97; §8, proof of Proposition 8.3, pp. 106–108
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21. Tau Ceti f790474 has the Frobenius prime sets (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean) but not the density theorem; its Chebotarev roadmap's Layer 10 plans it. Planned as in PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B.

prerequisites.why: The ordinary residually reducible deformation theory (local conditions, Propositions 3.9–4.18).

routes.title: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: analytic continuation of symmetric power functoriality along eigenvarieties
routes.brief: Build on Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions), whose ML.3 plans Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy as an endpoint but no layer plans the method that proves it. This Part II owns the first half of that method: moving automorphy of symmetric powers along irreducible components of eigenvarieties. Source: Newton–Thorne, 'Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021)). Its sequel (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B) and the Hilbert modular case (Newton–Thorne, Ann. of Math. 203 (2026)) should extend this Part II. Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 2.33: let (π_0, χ_0), (π′_0, χ′_0) be refined cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) whose points z_0, z′_0 of the tame level N, p-adic eigencurve lie on a common irreducible component, and n ≥ 2. If either (1) χ_0 is numerically non-critical and n-regular, (2) χ′_0 is n-regular, (3) the Zariski closures of r_{π_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) and r_{π′_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) contain SL_2 and (4) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic; or (1ord) χ_0 is ordinary, (2ord) π_0, π′_0 are not CM and (3ord) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic — then Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_0,ι} is automorphic. Theorem 3.1 (Theorem D): if Sym^{n−1} of one everywhere unramified cuspidal π_0 of weight ≥ 2 is automorphic, then so is Sym^{n−1} of every everywhere unramified cuspidal π of weight ≥ 2. Proposition 8.2: if π is non-CM of weight ≥ 2 with an n-regular accessible refinement at every ramified prime, Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic. Proposition 8.3 (congruences to forms with n-regular refinements). Together with Theorem E (owned by SymmetricPowersByUnitaryLevelRaising) these prove Theorems A and B, which ML.3 exports. Layers: (1) Lemma 2.2 (analytic continuation along irreducible components, after Conrad) and the rigid spaces of conjugate self-dual pseudocharacters with their absolutely irreducible loci, Azumaya algebras and tangent spaces (Lemmas 2.12–2.14); (2) the global trianguline tangent bound (Proposition 2.11), importing the vanishing of adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer groups (Newton–Thorne, JEMS) and Allen's genericity from PolarizedAutomorphyLifting; (3) symmetric power maps σ_n between pseudocharacter and character spaces, n-regular refinements (Definition 2.23), Theorem 2.24 (non-critical case), Theorem 2.27 (ordinary case), Corollary 2.28 and Lemma 2.29; (4) on the Coleman–Mazur eigencurve: the twin map and Lemma 2.32, Lemma 2.34 (trivialising families of characters over CM fields), the base-change morphism to a definite unitary eigenvariety and Theorem 2.33, and Lemma 2.35 (the bad locus is Zariski closed); (5) the 2-adic eigencurve at the boundary of weight space — Buzzard–Kilford's decomposition ℰ_0(b) = ⊔X_i with slope i·v(w) (Theorem 3.2) as an imported theorem, with the design job deciding whether it belongs as a later layer of PadicFamilies — and the ping-pong Lemmas 3.3–3.7 with Theorem 3.1; (6) killing ramification: Proposition 8.2, the Taylor–Wiles–Kisin argument of Proposition 8.3 with Lemma 8.4 (the non-regular locus is a principal divisor of the local lifting ring), and the final step of Theorem 8.1 through BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1. Imports: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions (PadicFamilies: L2 and L2a for the eigencurve, Buzzard's construction and Coleman classicality); Automorphic Galois Representations PartII (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII: AG2.2, AG2.3, AG2.5); Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison: ET.7a for unitary base change and descent); ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 (soluble descent) and ML.3 (endpoints); Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants: IHG.0–IHG.1); Global Galois deformation rings (GlobalGaloisDeformations: R04.1, G7); Local Galois deformation rings and their components (LocalGaloisDeformationRings: L7 for Fontaine–Laffaille); GL₂ Modularity Lifting (GL2ModularityLifting: R22.2–R22.3 for patching).
